data.title: Empty
data.tagline: Explain why no data is shown and what to do next
data.description: An empty state should not leave a blank area. Tell people what normally appears there, why it is empty now, and whether the next step is to create something, search, change a filter, or wait for data.

use: A new account with no records
Content removed or not yet available
avoid: Show only an illustration with no explanation
Blame the user for an empty result
Offer an action that cannot solve the empty state
Use the same message for first use, errors, and no search results

lessonPractice.title: A new team opens the project list for the first time. The request succeeded, but there are no projects. What should appear?

options.label: Keep the skeleton visible and let people infer that the list is empty
options.feedback: The request is finished, so a loading state incorrectly suggests that content is still on its way.

options.label: Say there are no projects yet and provide a Create project action
options.feedback: The page explains what belongs here, why it is empty now, and the useful next step for creating the first item.

options.label: Show a loading error and ask people to refresh the page
options.feedback: An empty successful response is not a failure. Refreshing repeats the request without solving the absence of data.

data.agentPrompt: When the project request succeeds with no items, show 'No projects yet' and a Create project action. Keep loading and request failure as separate states with appropriate feedback and retry. Simulate and verify all three states.

references.title: Designing Empty States in Complex Applications: 3 Guidelines
